questions.explanation: The caution about the findings follows from the sample's limits, a cause-and-effect relationship: "Consequently." Nonetheless would contradict that logic, and Similarly and In other words do not express consequence.

questions.passage: Bees pollinate many of the crops people depend on. ______ they contribute to the production of almonds, apples, and blueberries.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence names particular crops from the general claim, so it specifies: "Specifically." The other three signal contrast or an alternative condition.

questions.passage: The manuscript was long assumed to be a copy of a lost original. ______ chemical analysis of its ink shows it to be older than any known copy, raising the possibility that it is the original itself.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: New evidence overturns the old assumption, so a contrast is needed, and "recently" fits new analysis: B. Similarly and In addition would treat the finding as more of the same, and As a result would make it a consequence of the assumption.

questions.passage: First, preheat the oven to 350 degrees. ______ grease the baking pan.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: "First" begins a sequence, so the following step takes "Next." Finally would signal the last step, and However and Instead signal contrast.

questions.passage: The team practiced every day all summer. ______ they entered the season with confidence.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Confidence is the outcome of the summer's practice: "Consequently." Even so and On the contrary would present confidence as surprising or opposed, and For example does not fit.

questions.passage: Wolves were reintroduced to the park in 1995. ______ the elk population, which had grown unchecked for decades, began to decline.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The decline follows the reintroduction in time and as its effect; "Before long" carries that sequence. The other three signal contrast or an alternative.

questions.passage: The painter rarely dated her canvases. ______ scholars must rely on the evolution of her style to place them in sequence.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Because the paintings are undated, scholars must use style; that is a consequence: "Hence." Likewise signals similarity, Instead a replacement, and Meanwhile simultaneity.

questions.passage: Most of the town's residents work in the fishing industry. ______ a few commute to the city for office jobs.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence notes an exception to the first, a mild contrast: "Still." Consequently and Furthermore would present the commuters as following from or adding to the majority, and In short would summarize.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The monarch butterfly migrates up to 3,000 miles each fall.
• It travels from Canada and the United States to central Mexico.
• No single butterfly completes the round trip.
• The full journey takes several generations.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the length of the monarch's migration. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The monarch butterfly's migration takes several generations to complete.
Monarch butterflies migrate up to 3,000 miles each fall, from Canada and the United States to central Mexico.
No single monarch butterfly completes the round trip.
Monarch butterflies spend the winter in central Mexico.
questions.explanation: Length means distance, and only B gives the distance (3,000 miles) with its endpoints. A and C are about generations and individual butterflies, and D omits distance entirely.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Hedy Lamarr was a Hollywood film actress in the 1930s and 1940s.
• With the composer George Antheil, she patented a frequency-hopping radio system in 1942.
• The system was meant to keep radio-guided torpedoes from being jammed.
• Frequency-hopping ideas now underpin Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
questions.stem: The student wants to introduce Lamarr's invention and its lasting relevance to an audience unfamiliar with her. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Hedy Lamarr was a Hollywood film actress in the 1930s and 1940s.
Hedy Lamarr, better known as a 1940s film actress, co-patented a frequency-hopping system in 1942 whose ideas now underpin Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
Frequency hopping was designed to keep torpedoes from being jammed.
George Antheil was a composer who worked with Lamarr.
questions.explanation: An unfamiliar audience needs to be told who Lamarr was, what she invented, and why it still matters; B does all three. A stops at the acting career, C omits Lamarr, and D is about Antheil.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The city's recycling rate was 22 percent in 2015.
• In 2018 the city switched to single-stream bins, in which all recyclables go together.
• The recycling rate rose to 31 percent in 2019.
• Contamination (non-recyclable items in the bins) rose from 8 percent to 19 percent over the same period.
• Contaminated loads are sent to landfill.
questions.stem: The student wants to present a drawback of the switch to single-stream bins. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The city's recycling rate rose from 22 percent to 31 percent after 2018.
Since the switch to single-stream bins, contamination has more than doubled, and contaminated loads end up in landfill.
The city switched to single-stream bins in 2018.
Recycling rates are measured once a year.
questions.explanation: A drawback is a negative result, and only B presents one: more contamination, and contaminated loads landfilled. A is a benefit, C is neutral, and D is not from the notes.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Sea otters eat sea urchins.
• Sea urchins eat kelp.
• Where otters were hunted to local extinction, urchin numbers exploded and kelp forests vanished.
• Where otters have returned, kelp forests have recovered.
questions.stem: The student wants to explain the connection between sea otters and kelp forests. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Because otters keep urchin numbers in check and urchins eat kelp, kelp forests vanish where otters are lost and recover where they return.
Kelp forests are important habitats for many species.
Sea otters were once hunted for their fur.
questions.explanation: Explaining a connection requires the chain of cause and effect, which only B lays out. A gives one link, and C and D are not in the notes.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The school's robotics team was founded in 2019.
• It has 24 members.
• It won the state championship in 2024.
• It meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays after school.
questions.stem: The student wants to inform students of when the team meets. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The team won the state championship in 2024.
The robotics team meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays after school.
questions.explanation: Only B gives the meeting schedule.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Octavia Butler published her first novel in 1976.
• She wrote twelve novels in total.
• In 1995 she became the first science-fiction writer to receive a MacArthur Fellowship.
• Her novel Kindred is widely taught in schools.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the recognition Butler received for her work. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Octavia Butler wrote twelve novels over her career.
In 1995 Butler became the first science-fiction writer to be awarded a MacArthur Fellowship.
Butler's novel Kindred is widely taught in schools.
Butler published her first novel in 1976.
questions.explanation: Recognition means honors, and B names the honor and its significance (first in her genre). C is a form of recognition but weaker and less specific; A and D are facts about output, not recognition.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A 2022 trial gave 500 adults either a daily vitamin D supplement or a placebo for one year.
• Bone density did not differ between the two groups.
• The trial enrolled only adults whose vitamin D levels were normal at the start.
• Earlier studies of adults who were deficient in vitamin D found that supplements improved bone density.
questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the trial's result does not contradict the earlier studies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The 2022 trial found no difference in bone density between the groups.
Because the trial enrolled only adults whose vitamin D was already normal, its null result does not conflict with the benefits earlier studies found in deficient adults.
The trial lasted one year and included 500 adults.
Vitamin D supplements are widely available.
questions.explanation: The reconciliation is that the two sets of studies looked at different people: B says so. A states the result without reconciling it, C gives design details, and D is not in the notes.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is a region of floating plastic debris.
• It lies in the ocean between Hawaii and California.
• Estimates of its area range from 700,000 to 1.6 million square kilometers.
• Most of the plastic consists of tiny fragments rather than large items.
questions.stem: The student wants to correct a likely misconception about what the patch looks like. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The patch lies in the ocean between Hawaii and California.
Rather than a floating island of trash, the patch consists mostly of tiny plastic fragments spread across the water.
Estimates of the patch's area vary widely.
The patch is located in the Pacific Ocean.
questions.explanation: Correcting a misconception means naming the wrong picture and replacing it, which B does ("rather than a floating island"). The others state facts without addressing what people wrongly imagine.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The library's summer reading program runs from June 10 to August 15.
• Children who read ten books receive a free book.
• Sign-up is at the library's front desk.
• Last year 340 children participated.
questions.stem: The student wants to tell parents how to enroll a child in the program. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Last year 340 children participated in the program.
Children who read ten books receive a free book.
Parents can sign their children up at the library's front desk.
questions.explanation: Only C tells parents where to enroll.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In 1854 the British army hospital at Scutari had a death rate above 40 percent.
• Florence Nightingale reorganized sanitation at the hospital.
• By 1855 the death rate had fallen to about 2 percent.
• Nightingale presented her mortality data in a "coxcomb" diagram.
• The diagram helped persuade Parliament to reform army hospitals.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize how Nightingale's use of data brought about change. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The death rate at Scutari fell from above 40 percent to about 2 percent.
Nightingale's coxcomb diagram of hospital deaths helped persuade Parliament to reform army hospitals.
Nightingale reorganized sanitation at the Scutari hospital.
The army hospital was located at Scutari.
questions.explanation: The goal has two parts, data and change, and B links them: the diagram persuaded Parliament to reform. A gives the change without the data's role, and C and D omit data entirely.

questions.passage: The festival, which is held every ______ draws visitors from across the state.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The nonessential clause "which is held every August" was opened with a comma after "festival" and must be closed with a matching comma. A semicolon or colon would break the sentence, and no punctuation leaves the clause unclosed.

questions.passage: The team had a single goal for the ______ to finish the season without a serious injury.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "To finish the season without a serious injury" explains what the goal was and is not an independent clause. A colon introduces such an explanation. A semicolon needs an independent clause on both sides, and a comma or nothing would run the explanation into the sentence.

questions.passage: Volcanic soil is rich in ______ it is also prone to erosion.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined here without a conjunction, so a semicolon is required. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a colon would wrongly present the second clause as an explanation of the first.

questions.passage: The exhibit includes four of the artist's ______ portraits, a landscape, and an unfinished self-portrait.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The list "two portraits, a landscape, and an unfinished self-portrait" spells out what the four works are, so a colon introduces it. A comma would make "two portraits" read as a fifth item, a semicolon needs an independent clause after it, and no punctuation is a run-on.

questions.passage: Maya ______ who moved here last year, is running for city council.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The clause "who moved here last year" is nonessential and is closed by the comma before "is," so it must be opened by a comma after "Chen."

questions.passage: Whoever finishes the puzzle ______ a prize.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Whoever finishes the puzzle first" is the subject of the sentence, and no punctuation may separate a subject from its verb.

questions.passage: The committee reviewed the ______ then it voted.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Then" is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so it cannot join two independent clauses with only a comma; a semicolon is needed. No punctuation gives a run-on, and a colon would present the vote as an explanation of the review.

questions.passage: Three ______ the Ohio, the Missouri, and the Illinois—feed into the Mississippi from the east and the west.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The list of rivers is closed by a dash, so it must be opened by a dash; the pair sets off an appositive that contains its own commas. A comma, semicolon, or colon would not match the closing dash.

questions.passage: Because the roads were ______ the school opened two hours late.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: An introductory dependent clause ("Because the roads were icy") is followed by a comma. A semicolon or colon requires an independent clause before it, and no punctuation is a run-on.

questions.passage: The results were ______ every sample showed the same pattern.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The second clause explains the first (how the results were consistent), which is what a colon introduces. A comma alone is a comma splice, no punctuation is a run-on, and a semicolon with "and" is redundant and incorrect.

questions.passage: The lab's newest instrument, a mass ______ can identify compounds present in vanishingly small amounts.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "A mass spectrometer" is an appositive opened by the comma after "instrument," so it must be closed by a comma. A dash would need a matching opening dash, a semicolon would break the sentence, and no punctuation leaves the appositive open.

questions.passage: Students may choose one of two ______ a research paper or an oral presentation.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The phrase after the blank names the two options and is not an independent clause, so a colon introduces it. A semicolon requires an independent clause, and a comma or nothing runs the list into the sentence.

questions.passage: Each of the applicants ______ required to submit two references.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is "each," which is singular; "of the applicants" is a prepositional phrase and does not change the number. So the verb is "is."

questions.passage: The sculptures, along with the artist's notebooks, ______ on display until March.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is "sculptures," which is plural. A phrase beginning "along with" does not change the subject's number, so the verb is "are."

questions.passage: Neither the coach nor the players ______ satisfied with the result.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Players" is plural and nearer, so "were."

questions.passage: The data ______ that the treatment is effective in most cases.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: In formal usage "data" is a plural noun (the singular is "datum"), so it takes the plural verb "suggest." The other three are singular forms.

questions.passage: She has ______ the marathon three times.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: After the helping verb "has," the main verb takes its past participle: "run." "Ran" is the simple past, and "running" and "runs" cannot follow "has."

questions.passage: If the bridge ______ closed, we would have taken the ferry.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Would have taken" describes an unreal past situation, so the if-clause takes the past perfect: "had been closed."

questions.passage: The report, which ______ published last spring, has already shaped policy.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Which" refers to "the report," which is singular, and "last spring" places it in the past: "was."

questions.passage: Known for ______ precision, the company refuses to release any watch that loses more than a second a month.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "The company" is a singular noun, so the possessive pronoun is "its." "Their" is plural, "it's" means "it is," and "there" is not a possessive.

questions.passage: The students ______ finished early were allowed to leave.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the subject of "finished" and refers to people, so "who." "Whom" is an object form, "which" is for things, and "whose" is possessive.

questions.passage: Rarely ______ such a large crowd gathered in the square.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with "rarely," the helping verb comes before the subject. The subject is "crowd," which is singular, and "gathered" is a past participle, so the helping verb is "has."

questions.passage: To succeed in the course, ______
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: careful notes must be taken by students.
it is necessary that notes be taken carefully.
questions.explanation: The opening phrase "To succeed in the course" describes the students, so "students" must be the subject that follows it. In A, C, and D the phrase is left dangling, attached to notes, note-taking, or "it."

questions.passage: The committee will announce ______ decision on Friday.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Committee" is a singular noun, so the possessive is "its." "It's" means "it is," "their" is plural, and "there" is not possessive.

questions.stem: If 2x + 9 = 23, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 9 from both sides: 2x = 14. Divide by 2: x = 7.

questions.stem: If 6x + 14 = 86, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 14 from both sides: 6x = 72. Divide by 6: x = 12.

questions.stem: If 2x + 15 = 25, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 15 from both sides: 2x = 10. Divide by 2: x = 5.

questions.stem: What value of x satisfies 4(x + 5) = 8x − 16?
questions.explanation: Distribute: 4x + 20 = 8x − 16. Collect x terms: 36 = 4x, so x = 9. (A common slip is to forget to multiply 5 by 4 when distributing.)

questions.stem: What value of x satisfies 4(x + 1) = 5x − 2?
questions.explanation: Distribute: 4x + 4 = 5x − 2. Collect x terms: 6 = 1x, so x = 6. (A common slip is to forget to multiply 1 by 4 when distributing.)

questions.stem: What value of x satisfies 4(x + 4) = 7x + 1?
questions.explanation: Distribute: 4x + 16 = 7x + 1. Collect x terms: 15 = 3x, so x = 5. (A common slip is to forget to multiply 4 by 4 when distributing.)

questions.stem: 8 less than twice a number is 2 more than the number. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be n. "8 less than twice a number" is 2n − 8; "2 more than the number" is n + 2. Set them equal: 2n − 8 = n + 2, so n = 10.

questions.stem: 7 less than twice a number is 2 more than the number. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be n. "7 less than twice a number" is 2n − 7; "2 more than the number" is n + 2. Set them equal: 2n − 7 = n + 2, so n = 9.

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points (4, 2) and (7, -1) in the xy-plane?
questions.explanation: Slope = change in y over change in x = (-1 − 2) / (7 − 4) = -3/3 = -1. Reversing the subtraction in only one of the differences flips the sign, and dividing the other way gives the reciprocal.

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points (-4, 5) and (-1, 2) in the xy-plane?
questions.explanation: Slope = change in y over change in x = (2 − 5) / (-1 − -4) = -3/3 = -1. Reversing the subtraction in only one of the differences flips the sign, and dividing the other way gives the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A streaming service charges a one-time setup fee plus a fixed monthly rate. A customer paid $160 in total for the first 5 months and $208 in total for the first 7 months. What is the monthly rate, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The difference between the two totals covers 2 extra months: $208 − $160 = $48, so the monthly rate is 48/2 = $24. (Then the setup fee is $160 − 5·24 = $40.)

questions.stem: A streaming service charges a one-time setup fee plus a fixed monthly rate. A customer paid $136 in total for the first 4 months and $256 in total for the first 9 months. What is the monthly rate, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The difference between the two totals covers 5 extra months: $256 − $136 = $120, so the monthly rate is 120/5 = $24. (Then the setup fee is $136 − 4·24 = $40.)

questions.stem: A streaming service charges a one-time setup fee plus a fixed monthly rate. A customer paid $95 in total for the first 3 months and $125 in total for the first 5 months. What is the monthly rate, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The difference between the two totals covers 2 extra months: $125 − $95 = $30, so the monthly rate is 30/2 = $15. (Then the setup fee is $95 − 3·15 = $50.)

questions.stem: What is the x-intercept of the graph of 5x + 6y = 15 in the xy-plane?
questions.explanation: At the x-intercept, y = 0: 5x = 15, so x = 3. The point is (3, 0). Setting x = 0 instead gives the y-intercept, and (c, 0) forgets to divide by the coefficient.

questions.stem: In the xy-plane, a line passes through (4, 3) and is parallel to the line y = -1x + 6. What is the y-intercept of the first line?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines share a slope, so the line is y = -1x + b. Substitute (4, 3): 3 = -1·4 + b, so b = 3 − -4 = 7. The y-intercept is 7; 6 is the other line's intercept.

questions.stem: In the xy-plane, a line passes through (3, 2) and is parallel to the line y = -2x − 6. What is the y-intercept of the first line?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines share a slope, so the line is y = -2x + b. Substitute (3, 2): 2 = -2·3 + b, so b = 2 − -6 = 8. The y-intercept is 8; -6 is the other line's intercept.

questions.stem: If x + y = 12 and x − y = 6, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Add the two equations: 2x = 18, so x = 9. (Then y = 3.)

questions.stem: If x + y = 16 and x − y = 0, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Add the two equations: 2x = 16, so x = 8. (Then y = 8.)

questions.stem: A theater sold 37 tickets to a show. Adult tickets cost $12 and child tickets cost $8, and the total revenue was $376. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Let a be adult tickets and c child tickets. Then a + c = 37 and 12a + 8c = 376. From the first, c = 37 − a. Substitute: 12a + 8(37 − a) = 376, so 4a = 80, and a = 20. (17 is the number of child tickets.)

questions.stem: A theater sold 29 tickets to a show. Adult tickets cost $20 and child tickets cost $12, and the total revenue was $500. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Let a be adult tickets and c child tickets. Then a + c = 29 and 20a + 12c = 500. From the first, c = 29 − a. Substitute: 20a + 12(29 − a) = 500, so 8a = 152, and a = 19. (10 is the number of child tickets.)

questions.stem: A theater sold 57 tickets to a show. Adult tickets cost $20 and child tickets cost $12, and the total revenue was $996. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Let a be adult tickets and c child tickets. Then a + c = 57 and 20a + 12c = 996. From the first, c = 57 − a. Substitute: 20a + 12(57 − a) = 996, so 8a = 312, and a = 39. (18 is the number of child tickets.)

questions.stem:
The system of equations below has no solution. What is the value of k?

2x + 3y = 13
4x + ky = 29
questions.explanation: Lines with no common point are parallel: the second equation's coefficients must be a multiple of the first's. 4 is 2·2, so k must be 2·3 = 6; and 29 ≠ 2·13 = 26, so the lines are distinct rather than identical.

2x + 3y = 20
6x + ky = 62
questions.explanation: Lines with no common point are parallel: the second equation's coefficients must be a multiple of the first's. 6 is 3·2, so k must be 3·3 = 9; and 62 ≠ 3·20 = 60, so the lines are distinct rather than identical.

questions.stem: Which of the following values of x satisfies the inequality 3x − 3 > 12?
questions.explanation: Add 3: 3x > 15. Divide by 3: x > 5. The inequality is strict, so 5 itself does not work; the only listed value greater than 5 is 6.

questions.stem: Which of the following values of x satisfies the inequality 3x − 5 > 4?
questions.explanation: Add 5: 3x > 9. Divide by 3: x > 3. The inequality is strict, so 3 itself does not work; the only listed value greater than 3 is 4.

questions.stem: A club has $66 to spend on a party. The venue charges a flat $20 fee plus $9 per guest. What is the greatest number of guests the club can afford?
questions.explanation: With g guests the cost is 20 + 9g, which must be at most 66: 9g ≤ 46, so g ≤ 5.11111. The greatest whole number is 5. Ignoring the flat fee gives 7, which is too many.

questions.stem: A club has $65 to spend on a party. The venue charges a flat $25 fee plus $8 per guest. What is the greatest number of guests the club can afford?
questions.explanation: With g guests the cost is 25 + 8g, which must be at most 65: 8g ≤ 40, so g ≤ 5. The greatest whole number is 5. Ignoring the flat fee gives 8, which is too many.

questions.stem: What is the smallest integer value of x for which 6x − 6 ≥ 13?
questions.explanation: Add 6: 6x ≥ 19. Divide by 6: x ≥ 19/6. That is a little more than 3, so the smallest integer that satisfies it is 4.

questions.stem: What is the smallest integer value of x for which 6x − 8 ≥ 17?
questions.explanation: Add 8: 6x ≥ 25. Divide by 6: x ≥ 25/6. That is a little more than 4, so the smallest integer that satisfies it is 5.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (x − 4)(x − 2)?
questions.explanation: Multiply each term: x·x = x², x·(-2) + (-4)·x = -6x, and (-4)(-2) = 8. So the product is x² − 6x + 8. Sign slips on the middle or last term produce the wrong choices, and dropping the middle term entirely gives x² + 8.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (x + 4)(x − 2)?
questions.explanation: Multiply each term: x·x = x², x·(-2) + (4)·x = 2x, and (4)(-2) = -8. So the product is x² + 2x − 8. Sign slips on the middle or last term produce the wrong choices, and dropping the middle term entirely gives x² − 8.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (x − 6)(x − 2)?
questions.explanation: Multiply each term: x·x = x², x·(-2) + (-6)·x = -8x, and (-6)(-2) = 12. So the product is x² − 8x + 12. Sign slips on the middle or last term produce the wrong choices, and dropping the middle term entirely gives x² + 12.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a factor of x² + 3x − 10?
questions.explanation: Look for two numbers that multiply to -10 and add to 3: 5 and -2. So x² + 3x − 10 = (x + 5)(x − 2), and x − 2 is a factor.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a factor of x² + 1x − 30?
questions.explanation: Look for two numbers that multiply to -30 and add to 1: 6 and -5. So x² + 1x − 30 = (x + 6)(x − 5), and x − 5 is a factor.

questions.stem: For x ≠ 5, which expression is equivalent to (x² − 25) / (x − 5)?
questions.explanation: x² − 25 is a difference of squares: (x − 5)(x + 5). Dividing by x − 5 leaves x + 5.

questions.stem: For x ≠ 2, which expression is equivalent to (x² − 4) / (x − 2)?
questions.explanation: x² − 4 is a difference of squares: (x − 2)(x + 2). Dividing by x − 2 leaves x + 2.

questions.stem: If x² = 64 and x > 0, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: The positive square root of 64 is 8.

questions.stem: If x² = 25 and x > 0, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: The positive square root of 25 is 5.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the solutions to x² − 13x + 30 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factor: (x − 3)(x − 10) = 0, so the solutions are 3 and 10, and their sum is 13. (Shortcut: for x² + bx + c = 0 the solutions sum to −b.) The product of the solutions is 30, not the sum.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the solutions to x² − 12x + 32 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factor: (x − 4)(x − 8) = 0, so the solutions are 4 and 8, and their sum is 12. (Shortcut: for x² + bx + c = 0 the solutions sum to −b.) The product of the solutions is 32, not the sum.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the solutions to x² − 11x + 28 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factor: (x − 4)(x − 7) = 0, so the solutions are 4 and 7, and their sum is 11. (Shortcut: for x² + bx + c = 0 the solutions sum to −b.) The product of the solutions is 28, not the sum.

questions.stem: The equation x² − 10x + c = 0 has exactly one real solution. What is the value of c?
questions.explanation: One real solution means the discriminant is zero: b² − 4ac = 10² − 4c = 0, so c = 100/4 = 25. Check: x² − 10x + 25 = (x − 5)².

questions.stem: The equation x² − 4x + c = 0 has exactly one real solution. What is the value of c?
questions.explanation: One real solution means the discriminant is zero: b² − 4ac = 4² − 4c = 0, so c = 16/4 = 4. Check: x² − 4x + 4 = (x − 2)².

questions.stem: A colony of bacteria starts with 2,000 cells and grows by 8% each hour. Which function models the number of cells N(t) after t hours?
questions.explanation: A 8% increase per hour multiplies the count by 1.08 each hour, so after t hours it is 2,000 × 1.08ᵗ. Multiplying by 0.08 would shrink it, adding 8t is linear growth, and multiplying by 8 is 800% growth.

questions.stem: A colony of bacteria starts with 2,000 cells and grows by 6% each hour. Which function models the number of cells N(t) after t hours?
questions.explanation: A 6% increase per hour multiplies the count by 1.06 each hour, so after t hours it is 2,000 × 1.06ᵗ. Multiplying by 0.06 would shrink it, adding 6t is linear growth, and multiplying by 6 is 600% growth.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 2x + 5. What is the minimum value of f(x)?
questions.explanation: The parabola opens upward, so the minimum is at the vertex, x = −b/(2a) = 2/2 = 1. Then f(1) = 1 − 2 + 5 = 4. The x-coordinate 1 and the constant term 5 are the tempting wrong answers.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 10x + 24. What is the minimum value of f(x)?
questions.explanation: The parabola opens upward, so the minimum is at the vertex, x = −b/(2a) = 10/2 = 5. Then f(5) = 25 − 50 + 24 = -1. The x-coordinate 5 and the constant term 24 are the tempting wrong answers.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 2x + 8. What is the minimum value of f(x)?
questions.explanation: The parabola opens upward, so the minimum is at the vertex, x = −b/(2a) = 2/2 = 1. Then f(1) = 1 − 2 + 8 = 7. The x-coordinate 1 and the constant term 8 are the tempting wrong answers.

questions.stem: A sample of a radioactive substance has a mass of 320 grams and a half-life of 3 years. What will its mass be, in grams, after 12 years?
questions.explanation: 12 years is 4 half-lives. Each half-life halves the mass: 320 → 160 → 80 → 40 → 20. After 4 halvings the mass is 20 grams.

questions.stem: A sample of a radioactive substance has a mass of 160 grams and a half-life of 6 years. What will its mass be, in grams, after 24 years?
questions.explanation: 24 years is 4 half-lives. Each half-life halves the mass: 160 → 80 → 40 → 20 → 10. After 4 halvings the mass is 10 grams.

questions.explanation: Set the expressions equal: x² = 3x, so x² − 3x = 0 and x(x − 3) = 0. The x-coordinates are 0 and 3, which sum to 3.

questions.skill: Systems of equations in two variables
questions.stem: How many points of intersection do the graphs of y = x² + 2 and y = 7 have in the xy-plane?
questions.explanation: Set x² + 2 = 7, so x² = 5. Since 5 is positive, x = ±√5: two solutions, so two intersection points. There would be one if 7 equaled 2 (the vertex) and none if 7 were less than 2.

questions.skill: Systems of equations in two variables

questions.explanation: 8 parts white is 4 times the 2 in the ratio, so the blue must be 4 times 3: 12. Equivalently, 3/2 = x/8 gives x = 12.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units

questions.explanation: Convert minutes to hours: 40 minutes = 2/3 hour. Distance = 90 × 2/3 = 60 miles. Multiplying by 40 without converting gives 3600, which is far too large.

questions.explanation: Convert minutes to hours: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Distance = 72 × 1/3 = 24 miles. Multiplying by 20 without converting gives 1440, which is far too large.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.stem: A 64-milliliter solution is made of alcohol and water in the ratio 3 : 5. How many milliliters of alcohol does it contain?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 8 parts in all, so each part is 64/8 = 8 mL. Alcohol is 3 parts: 3 × 8 = 24 mL. (40 mL is the water.)

questions.stem: A pair of shoes regularly priced at $120 is on sale for 25% off. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: 25% of $120 is $30, so the sale price is $120 − $30 = $90. $30 is the discount itself, and subtracting 25 dollars instead of 25 percent is a common slip.

questions.stem: A pair of shoes regularly priced at $240 is on sale for 20% off. What is the sale price?

questions.stem: The number of students in a club increased from 50 to 75. By what percent did the membership increase?
questions.explanation: Percent increase = (change) / (original) × 100 = (75 − 50) / 50 × 100 = 25/50 × 100 = 50%. Dividing by the new value instead of the original gives 33%.

questions.stem: The number of students in a club increased from 40 to 50. By what percent did the membership increase?
questions.explanation: Percent increase = (change) / (original) × 100 = (50 − 40) / 40 × 100 = 10/40 × 100 = 25%. Dividing by the new value instead of the original gives 20%.

questions.stem: The number of students in a club increased from 120 to 150. By what percent did the membership increase?
questions.explanation: Percent increase = (change) / (original) × 100 = (150 − 120) / 120 × 100 = 30/120 × 100 = 25%. Dividing by the new value instead of the original gives 20%.

questions.stem: After a 20% discount, a jacket costs $60. What was the original price of the jacket?
questions.explanation: A 20% discount leaves 80% of the original: 0.80 × original = 60, so original = 60 / 0.80 = $75. Adding 20% to the sale price ($72) is wrong because 20% of the smaller sale price is less than 20% of the original.

questions.stem: After a 25% discount, a jacket costs $60. What was the original price of the jacket?
questions.explanation: A 25% discount leaves 75% of the original: 0.75 × original = 60, so original = 60 / 0.75 = $80. Adding 25% to the sale price ($75) is wrong because 25% of the smaller sale price is less than 25% of the original.

What is the median of the list?
questions.explanation: Order the values: 12, 26, 31, 42, 43, 45. With six values the median is the average of the third and fourth: (31 + 42) / 2 = 73/2. Taking just one of the middle values, or computing the mean (199/6), gives a wrong answer.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.stem: The mean of 5 numbers is 12. When one more number is added to the list, the mean of the 6 numbers is 15. What is the number that was added?
questions.explanation: Mean × count = total. The 5 numbers total 5 × 12 = 60; the 6 numbers total 6 × 15 = 90. The added number is the difference: 90 − 60 = 30.

questions.stem: A scatterplot shows the relationship between the number of hours a student studies, h, and score on a test, s. The line of best fit is s = 2.5h + 50. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number 2.5 in this equation?
choices: The predicted value of the second variable when the first is 0 is 2.5.
The first variable increases by 2.5 for each 1-unit increase in the second.
For each 1-unit increase in the first variable, the model predicts a increase of 2.5 in the second.
The maximum predicted value of the second variable is 2.5.
questions.explanation: In a linear model the coefficient of the input variable is the slope: the change in the output for each 1-unit change in the input. 50 is the intercept (the prediction when the input is 0), and the slope does not describe a maximum or run in the other direction.

questions.stem: A scatterplot shows the relationship between the age of a used car in years, a, and its price in thousands of dollars, p. The line of best fit is p = 20 − 3a. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number 3 in this equation?
choices: The first variable decreases by 3 for each 1-unit increase in the second.
For each 1-unit increase in the first variable, the model predicts a decrease of 3 in the second.
The maximum predicted value of the second variable is 3.
The predicted value of the second variable when the first is 0 is 3.
questions.explanation: In a linear model the coefficient of the input variable is the slope: the change in the output for each 1-unit change in the input. 20 is the intercept (the prediction when the input is 0), and the slope does not describe a maximum or run in the other direction.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.stem: A random sample of 250 residents of a town with 2,000 residents found that 30% of the sample use the public library at least once a month. Based on the sample, which is the best estimate of the number of residents in the town who use the library at least once a month?
questions.explanation: A random sample's proportion is the best estimate for the whole population: 30% of 2,000 = 600. Applying 30% to the sample (75) answers a different question.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.stem: A random sample of 500 residents of a town with 5,000 residents found that 40% of the sample use the public library at least once a month. Based on the sample, which is the best estimate of the number of residents in the town who use the library at least once a month?
questions.explanation: A random sample's proportion is the best estimate for the whole population: 40% of 5,000 = 2,000. Applying 40% to the sample (200) answers a different question.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.stem: A poll of a random sample of voters estimates that 63% support a ballot measure, with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
choices: 4% of the voters polled changed their minds.
The poll surveyed 4% of all voters.
Exactly 63% of all voters support the measure.
It is plausible that between 59% and 67% of all voters support the measure.
questions.explanation: A margin of error gives a range of plausible values for the population: 63 ± 4, or 59% to 67%. It does not make the sample estimate exact, and it says nothing about voters changing their minds or about how many were surveyed.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.stem: A poll of a random sample of voters estimates that 63% support a ballot measure, with a margin of error of 5 percentage points. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
choices: Exactly 63% of all voters support the measure.
5% of the voters polled changed their minds.
The poll surveyed 5% of all voters.
It is plausible that between 58% and 68% of all voters support the measure.
questions.explanation: A margin of error gives a range of plausible values for the population: 63 ± 5, or 58% to 68%. It does not make the sample estimate exact, and it says nothing about voters changing their minds or about how many were surveyed.

questions.stem: A researcher wants to estimate the average number of hours per week that students at a large university spend on homework. Which sampling method is most likely to produce a sample that represents the whole student body?
choices: Surveying every student in one large chemistry lecture
Posting a survey online and using the first 300 responses
Selecting 300 students at random from a list of all enrolled students
Surveying the 300 students who attend a study-skills workshop
questions.explanation: Only random selection from the full list gives every student an equal chance of being chosen. The other methods draw from groups likely to differ from the student body: workshop attendees, one course's students, or people who choose to respond.

questions.stem: A study found that people who drink coffee every morning score higher on memory tests than people who do not. Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the conclusion that coffee improves memory?
choices: The study included more than 1,000 participants.
Participants who drank coffee reported enjoying it.
The memory tests were scored by researchers who did not know which participants drank coffee.
People who drink coffee every morning also sleep more regularly, and regular sleep is known to improve memory.
questions.explanation: The study is observational, so a third factor linked to both coffee drinking and memory could explain the result. Regular sleep is exactly such a factor. A large sample and blind scoring strengthen the study, and enjoyment is irrelevant.

questions.stem: A school wants to test whether a new tutoring program raises math scores. Which study design would best support a conclusion that the program causes higher scores?
choices: Survey students in the program about whether they feel more confident in math.
Randomly assign half of the interested students to the program and half to a waiting list, then compare their scores at the end of the term.
Compare the scores of students who chose to join the program with those who did not.
Offer the program to the students with the lowest scores and see whether their scores rise.
questions.explanation: Random assignment is what allows a causal conclusion, because it makes the two groups alike in everything except the program. Students who choose the program may differ from those who don't, the lowest scorers would likely rise anyway, and confidence is not a score.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 10 inches and a height of 5 inches. What is the area of the triangle, in square inches?
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 5 = 25. Forgetting the ½ gives 50.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a length of 9 centimeters and a width of 6 centimeters. What is the area of the rectangle, in square centimeters?
questions.explanation: Area of a rectangle = length × width = 9 × 6 = 54. The perimeter, 2(9 + 6) = 30, is a different measure.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 12 inches and a height of 9 inches. What is the area of the triangle, in square inches?
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 12 × 9 = 54. Forgetting the ½ gives 108.

questions.stem: A rectangular box has a length of 7 inches, a width of 8 inches, and a height of 4 inches. What is the volume of the box, in cubic inches?
questions.explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 7 × 8 × 4 = 224. The surface area, 2(7·8 + 7·4 + 8·4) = 232, is a different quantity.

questions.stem: A right circular cylinder has a radius of 4 and a height of 8. What is the volume of the cylinder?
questions.explanation: Volume of a cylinder = πr²h = π(4²)(8) = 128π. Using r instead of r² gives 32π.

questions.stem: The circumference of a circle is 14π. What is the area of the circle, in terms of π? (Enter the coefficient of π.)
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 14π, so r = 7. Area = πr² = 49π. The answer is the coefficient, 49.

questions.stem: The circumference of a circle is 16π. What is the area of the circle, in terms of π? (Enter the coefficient of π.)
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 16π, so r = 8. Area = πr² = 64π. The answer is the coefficient, 64.

questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle measure 42° and 44°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle sum to 180°: 180 − 42 − 44 = 94.

questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle measure 46° and 39°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle sum to 180°: 180 − 46 − 39 = 95.

questions.stem: In a triangle, two interior angles measure 37° and 47°. What is the measure of the exterior angle at the third vertex?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 37 + 47 = 84°. Equivalently, the third interior angle is 96°, and its exterior angle is 180 − 96 = 84°.

questions.stem: In a triangle, two interior angles measure 55° and 31°. What is the measure of the exterior angle at the third vertex?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 55 + 31 = 86°. Equivalently, the third interior angle is 94°, and its exterior angle is 180 − 94 = 86°.

questions.stem: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF, with AB corresponding to DE. AB = 4, BC = 6, and DE = 16. What is the length of EF?
questions.explanation: Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional. The scale factor from ABC to DEF is DE/AB = 16/4 = 4, so EF = 4 × BC = 4 × 6 = 24.

questions.stem: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF, with AB corresponding to DE. AB = 3, BC = 4, and DE = 6. What is the length of EF?
questions.explanation: Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional. The scale factor from ABC to DEF is DE/AB = 6/3 = 2, so EF = 2 × BC = 2 × 4 = 8.

questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 25 and one leg of length 7. What is the length of the other leg?
questions.explanation: Pythagorean theorem: 7² + leg² = 25², so leg² = 625 − 49 = 576 and the leg is 24. Subtracting the lengths themselves (25 − 7) is a common error.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of length 8 and 15. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: Pythagorean theorem: hypotenuse² = 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289, so the hypotenuse is √289 = 17.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of length 7 and 24. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: Pythagorean theorem: hypotenuse² = 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625, so the hypotenuse is √625 = 25.

questions.stem: In right triangle PQR, the right angle is at Q, PQ = 8, QR = 6, and PR = 10. What is the value of cos of angle P?
questions.explanation: For angle P, the opposite side is QR = 6, the adjacent side is PQ = 8, and the hypotenuse is PR = 10. cos P = adjacent/hypotenuse = 8/10 = 4/5.

questions.stem: In right triangle PQR, the right angle is at Q, PQ = 12, QR = 5, and PR = 13. What is the value of sin of angle P?
questions.explanation: For angle P, the opposite side is QR = 5, the adjacent side is PQ = 12, and the hypotenuse is PR = 13. sin P = opposite/hypotenuse = 5/13 = 5/13.

questions.stem: In a right triangle, one of the acute angles has a sine of 7/25. What is the cosine of the same angle? (Enter a fraction.)
questions.explanation: sin = opposite/hypotenuse = 7/25, so the opposite leg is 7 (up to scale) and the hypotenuse is 25. The adjacent leg is √(25² − 7²) = 24, so cos = adjacent/hypotenuse = 24/25.

questions.stem: In a right triangle, one of the acute angles has a sine of 12/20. What is the cosine of the same angle? (Enter a fraction.)
questions.explanation: sin = opposite/hypotenuse = 12/20, so the opposite leg is 12 (up to scale) and the hypotenuse is 20. The adjacent leg is √(20² − 12²) = 16, so cos = adjacent/hypotenuse = 16/20.

questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 6. What is its circumference?
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 2π(6) = 12π. 36π is the area.

questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 7. What is its circumference?
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 2π(7) = 14π. 49π is the area.

questions.stem: Which equation represents a circle in the xy-plane with center (-5, -4) and radius 4?
questions.explanation: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r². With h = -5, k = -4, r = 4: (x + 5)² + (y + 4)² = 16. Watch the signs inside the parentheses and remember the right side is r², not r.

questions.stem: Which equation represents a circle in the xy-plane with center (3, 4) and radius 3?
questions.explanation: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r². With h = 3, k = 4, r = 3: (x − 3)² + (y − 4)² = 9. Watch the signs inside the parentheses and remember the right side is r², not r.

questions.stem: A circle in the xy-plane has the equation x² + y² + 4x + 2y = 4. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x² + 4x becomes (x + 2)² − 4, and y² + 2y becomes (y + 1)² − 1. So (x + 2)² + (y + 1)² = 4 + 4 + 1 = 9, and the radius is √9 = 3. 9 is the radius squared.

questions.stem: A circle in the xy-plane has the equation x² + y² + 8x + 6y = 0. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x² + 8x becomes (x + 4)² − 16, and y² + 6y becomes (y + 3)² − 9. So (x + 4)² + (y + 3)² = 0 + 16 + 9 = 25, and the radius is √25 = 5. 25 is the radius squared.
